app.name: Bariga Land Intelligence
app.purpose: A small educational prototype that combines indicative land asking-price information with observed NDBI-based development measurements for five selected Bariga ward study areas.
app.builder: Built by Unekwuojo as a GeoRAD Academy Emerging Spatial Professional mentorship project, using the GeoRAD Land Intelligence starter and the student's Sprint 1–4 outputs.
app.study_area: Five selected ward polygons associated with Bariga, Shomolu, Lagos: Ibuowo / Owotutu, Ilaje, Pedro / Gbagada, Aiyetoro / Mafowoku, and Owode / Orile Bariga.
app.workflow: Sprint 1 prepared ward polygons; Sprint 2 collected indicative asking-price evidence; Sprint 3 summarized the market signal; Sprint 4 used satellite imagery and an NDBI-based proxy to compare observed development measurements for 2016 and 2026; Sprint 5 integrates both signals in a searchable web map.
features: Search a supported ward by its full name.
Select a ward from the location list or click its map marker/polygon.
View indicative market level, source and date searched.
View 2016 and 2026 development measurements, the calculated change and the supplied change level.
Switch between light and dark themes.
Ask this small local FAQ chatbot how to use the application and what its data means.
benefits: Brings two different spatial signals together in one place.
Makes it easier to inspect differences between the five study wards.
Demonstrates a reproducible workflow from GIS data and analysis outputs to a usable web prototype.
Can support early exploration and discussion, but is not a property valuation or investment recommendation.
limitations: Market prices are indicative asking-price values, not verified transaction prices or formal valuations.
There is only one market observation per ward in the provided market dataset; this is not enough to establish a robust market average or distribution.
NDBI is a built-up proxy and not a direct count of buildings. Negative changes do not automatically prove that buildings were removed.
The 2026 satellite comparison is year-to-date rather than a complete calendar year.
Aiyetoro / Mafowoku's 100% development measurement in both years needs further validation.
All five supplied development-change levels are Low under the current sprint methodology; interpret that categorical label cautiously.
This prototype only supports the five loaded wards. Other locations are outside its dataset.
how_to_use: Type the full ward name in the search field and press Enter or click Search.
Choose a ward from the Locations list to focus the map and display its details.
Click a ward polygon or map marker to open its popup and details.
Use Reset view to clear the selection and show all five wards.
Use the sun/moon button to switch between light and dark mode.
Open the help/chat button at the lower-right corner and ask a question about the app.

faq.a: This prototype was built by Abah James Unekwuojo for the GeoRAD Academy Emerging Spatial Professional mentorship, using the GeoRAD Land Intelligence starter and his Sprint 1–4 outputs.
It is a small map-based prototype that brings together an indicative land asking-price signal and an observed development-change signal for five selected Bariga wards.

faq.q: How do I search for a ward?
faq.a: Enter the ward's full name in the search field and press Enter or select Search. You can also select a ward in the Locations list.

faq.q: What does indicative market level mean?
faq.a: It is the selected asking-price figure per square metre used by the sprint workflow. It is indicative, based on the supplied listings, and should not be treated as a formal valuation or verified sale price.

It is the difference between the notebook's measured development percentages for 2016 and 2026, expressed in percentage points. It describes the supplied analysis output, not a prediction of future development.
NDBI is the Normalized Difference Built-up Index. In this project it is used as a proxy for built-up conditions, not as a direct count of buildings.

The supplied analysis calculates Recent Development minus Earlier Development. A negative value means the recent measured percentage is lower than the earlier value under this workflow. It does not, by itself, prove that buildings were removed.

faq.q: Can I use this for a property purchase?
faq.a: No. It is an educational prototype with limited asking-price observations and satellite-derived proxy measurements. Verify any property and seek qualified valuation/legal advice before making decisions.

faq.q: Why does a place show Town not available?
faq.a: The app currently contains only five supported ward records. Search using one of their full names. Other locations are outside the app's current dataset.

The work was split across sprints: QGIS/GeoJSON ward preparation, AI-assisted market-data collection, market-level summarization, a GeoRAD Google Earth Engine/Colab satellite workflow, then a JSON integration and Leaflet web map.
